display_name: The Three Patrons Parish (Pennyburn / Carnhill / Galliagh)
operator_notes: Joomla Dropfiles — cloud ↓ icon (a.mod_downloadlink) serves Word .docx.
Click the cloud on this Sunday's row — harvester converts docx → PDF automatically.
Do not record diocese GDPR/Privacy PDFs — only mod_downloadlink on the parish host.
do_not: Do not save a download URL from downandconnor.org or other diocese admin PDFs.
Do not use Pick bulletin image — this is a file download site.
operator_notes_2026_08_10: NOT a genuine dead-end — the earlier 'bot-blocked, no unprotected path' verdict
was WRONG and is superseded. threepatrons.org fronts its whole origin (listing
page AND the Joomla Dropfiles download route itself, e.g.
index.php?option=com_dropfiles&task=frontfile.download&...) with a SiteGround
'sg-captcha' challenge returning HTTP 202/303-to-home or 403 — but it is
PROBABILISTIC, not a hard block: direct plain HTTP requests (curl/urllib, no
browser) got through with the real file roughly 1 attempt in 5-10 across
repeated manual testing. A full Playwright headless browser navigation to the
exact same URL failed 0/20 times in a row in the same test session — the
browser's TLS/JS fingerprint is flagged far more consistently than a bare
HTTP client, which is why the old click+page.goto prediction fallback
(_try_dropfiles_predicted_downloads) never worked even though the underlying
file was never actually unreachable.
FIX: _try_dropfiles_predicted_downloads now retries via plain urllib (off the
event loop) instead of page.goto — first re-fetching the listing page itself
to read the REAL newest mod_downloadlink href (preferred over guessing),
falling back to sequential-ID prediction (predict_dropfiles_bulletin_urls)
only if the listing can't be fetched in budget, with the old browser-based
probe kept as a final tier 3 safety net.
Confirmed 2026-08-10 via direct curl: /files/10/Weekly-Bulletins/112/... 200s
with Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="Sunday 9th August 2026.pdf" —
a real, current, 2-page bulletin ("Nineteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time") — item
112 matches the site's own listing (110=26 July, 111=2 Aug, 112=9 Aug).
